Breaking News Desk: Coastal Resilience Funding Review

By Zachary J. Blum — BlackSheep Patriots News • Developing story format

Federal regulators are reviewing a new coastal resilience funding package after repeated severe spring storms along the East Coast raised pressure on infrastructure, insurance markets, flood defenses, emergency planning, and shoreline protection. For Atlantic City and South Jersey, the issue is not abstract. Coastal flooding, storm surge, beach erosion, drainage, road access, insurance costs, and tourism disruption can all become local economic issues.

This developing story matters because any fast-tracked funding could affect construction jobs, municipal planning, seawall and dune projects, drainage systems, beach replenishment, and long-term decisions about where public money goes. Local governments and residents should watch for grant announcements, eligibility rules, project lists, timelines, and whether funding reaches high-risk neighborhoods as well as high-visibility tourism zones.

Local Impact

Atlantic City

Flood defenses, beach access, tourism protection, roads, and public infrastructure could be affected.

Economy

Construction Jobs

Major resilience packages can create engineering, contracting, labor, and planning work.

Insurance

Cost Pressure

Flood risk and storm damage can influence premiums, lending, and property costs.

Watch Next

Official Docs

Track agency releases, city statements, project lists, and funding deadlines.

Verification note: Treat this as a developing public-interest story until official agency documents, municipal statements, or funding notices are linked directly.

Suggested sources to rotate: FEMA, NOAA, New Jersey DEP, City of Atlantic City, NWS Mount Holly, local emergency-management updates.

Earth’s health is not one number. It is the combined condition of the atmosphere, oceans, water systems, underground geology, tectonic plates, ice shelves, forests, wildlife, and space weather. Founder Biography Preview

Zachary J. Blum — BigRooster built BlackSheep Patriots News from survival, loss, fatherhood, faith, mistakes, rebuilding, and the belief that truth matters more than comfort.

Read Full Biography

Biography: Becoming BigRooster — The Full Story of Zachary J. Blum

Founder Biography • BlackSheep Patriots News / BigRooster Media

Zachary J. Blum — BigRooster is the founder of BlackSheep Patriots News and BigRooster Media. His story is built from survival, fatherhood, grief, mistakes, accountability, rebuilding, faith, and the mission behind an independent media platform rooted in Atlantic City and South Jersey.

Mission Statement: Truth Over Comfort. No corporate backing. No political affiliation. No filter. Just real, community-rooted reporting from someone who has lived enough life to know the difference between what is shown — and what is actually real.

Biography Photo Gallery

Early Life

I was born in Ilion, New York in September 1989. From the beginning, life did not come slow or easy — it came fast, unpredictable, and heavy. At five years old, I moved with my mother to Canton, New York. That is where I grew up tough: playing football, lacrosse, hockey, riding dirt bikes, snowmobiles, four-wheelers, and anything with wheels or an engine. I lived outside, constantly moving, learning early that staying still was not an option.

In 2002, everything shifted. We moved to Greenville, South Carolina. It was a different environment and a different energy. Something in me never fully settled there, and the pressure of trying to find belonging at a young age pushed me toward hard lessons.

Hard Lessons and Turning Points

At 14 years old, trying to find identity, structure, and protection in a place that did not feel like home, I became involved with a gang in the Greenville area. At that age, it felt like loyalty and purpose. Looking back, it was a dangerous path that came with consequences, lessons, and realities I had to face head-on.

By August 25, 2005, at just fifteen years old, I made one of the biggest decisions of my life. I left my mother’s house and went back to Herkimer, New York to live with my father, Keith Blum. My aunt and uncle, Darlene Brewer and Dale Brewer Sr., helped me make that turning point happen.

Friends, Music, and Loss

Back in Herkimer, I found my people. Johnathan “Nabby” Nabinger and Raymond Pinney were not just friends — we were together every day. We grew up side by side through our teenage years and into our early twenties. Raymond and I spent years making rap music, building something creative out of where we came from.

Losing Nabby in 2014 and Raymond in 2016 hit deeply. Those losses were not just moments; they were turning points. They shaped how I move, how I think, and how I carry everything forward.

Fatherhood

In 2010, my son Miguel was born in Ilion, New York. His mother and I raised him together as a co-parenting team, even while living separate lives. For the first nine years of his life, I was consistently present — showing up, learning what it meant to be a father, and doing my part alongside his mother to raise him the best we could.

Over time, things became unstable. After the loss of my twin sons in 2016, my life took a turn. Mentally, emotionally, and environmentally, I was not in a place that I felt was right for raising a child the way he deserved. I made one of the hardest decisions of my life and stepped back so Miguel could have stability with his mother full-time. Not because I did not love him — but because I did.

Loss Upon Loss

In 2016, my identical twin sons — Zachary John Blum Jr. and Zain Xavier Blum — were born on May 5, 2016. They passed away the same day. There are no words that fully explain that kind of pain. It is not something you simply move past; it becomes part of you.

Then in January 2019, my nephews died in a house fire in Herkimer, New York. Loss stacked on loss, year after year. The kind of weight that breaks most people. I did not break.

The Raleigh Decision

After everything I had been through, I called my father, Keith Blum, and asked him for help getting out. He bought me a Greyhound bus ticket to Charlotte, North Carolina. At around 5:25 in the morning in Raleigh, I was sitting there with that ticket — and something in me said: stop.

I walked to the counter and asked, “How much is a ticket to Myrtle Beach?” It was thirty-three dollars. I took it. That decision changed my life. I landed in Myrtle Beach, found two jobs, got stable, and started rebuilding from nothing.

More Trials and the Road Back

In October 2019, someone I was close with, Khrystina, stopped responding. Days later, I saw her face tied to a story about a murdered newborn. She had told me the baby was mine. The timeline matched. I contacted law enforcement, was brought in, questioned, and left carrying even more weight.

Life became movement again — New York, Myrtle Beach, Florida, kitchens, construction, hard labor, and survival. In October 2021, I returned to New York, made mistakes, and paid for them. I served a year in state prison and completed parole. Then I got back to work.

In early August 2025, I was involved in a motorcycle accident that disrupted everything. I still kept going, working at a Walmart Distribution Center through August and September. Stopping has never been an option.

Atlantic City and the Mission

After everything, I reconnected with Jordan. I told her there was nothing left for me where I was. She asked where I wanted to go. I did not know that night, but I woke up the next morning with the answer: Atlantic City, New Jersey. We got on a train and made the move. No guarantees. No safety net. Just belief.

In Atlantic City, I built BlackSheep Patriots News from the ground up. No funding. No team. No backing. Just me. I designed it, wrote it, built it, and published it. At the same time, I returned to school, pursuing communications while actively living it every day.

Before that, I built an audience through AI-driven video content. Now BigRooster Media operates across journalism, video, commentary, merchandise, music, and independent media as a full brand rooted in South Jersey.

WE UP

Everything I have been through — bad decisions, loss, pain, survival, rebuilding — built the foundation for what I am doing now. I do not speak from theory. I speak from experience.

This is not a finished story. I am still building. Still moving. Still becoming. WE UP.

Faith In Action

2. Pray

3. Serve

Faith Article: Strength Without Pretending Life Is Easy

Faith does not mean life stops hurting. Faith means pain does not get the final word. A person can carry grief, mistakes, regret, pressure, and responsibility while still choosing to stand up, rebuild, and become useful to others.

This faith section belongs on the site because news can be heavy. People need truth, but they also need encouragement. A strong media platform can report hard realities while still reminding readers that they are not powerless, not forgotten, and not finished.

For BlackSheep Patriots News, faith is not used as a weapon. It is a foundation: discipline, humility, gratitude, courage, service, responsibility, family, and the belief that God can still build something meaningful out of broken seasons.

Faith desk note: Scripture wording may vary by translation. Readers are encouraged to open their Bible, pray, serve, and seek trusted pastoral or professional support when carrying heavy grief, addiction, crisis, or mental-health pressure.

Coastal Resilience Funding Review

By Zachary J. Blum — BlackSheep Patriots News

Federal regulators are reviewing a new coastal resilience funding package after repeated severe spring storms along the East Coast raised pressure on flood defenses, emergency planning, infrastructure, insurance markets, and shoreline protection.

For Atlantic City and South Jersey, this is not just a federal policy story. It affects roads, drainage, beach access, dune systems, tourism, public works, construction jobs, and the long-term cost of living near the coast.

If funding moves forward, local residents should watch which projects are prioritized, which neighborhoods are protected, and whether money reaches high-risk areas beyond tourism corridors. Coastal resilience can create jobs and protect property, but only if funding is transparent and tied to real local needs.

What to watch next: FEMA notices, NOAA updates, New Jersey DEP announcements, city statements, grant deadlines, project lists, and local emergency-management briefings.

Verification note: This story should be updated with direct official links as funding documents become available.

Atlantic City This Week: Events, Restaurants, Weather & Public Safety

By Zachary J. Blum — BlackSheep Patriots News

Atlantic City enters the week with the same mix that defines the shore: tourism, local business, weather, entertainment, public safety, and neighborhood movement all happening at once. The Boardwalk, restaurants, casinos, and beach traffic remain central to how the city feels day by day.

Restaurant highlights this week include classic local stops and higher-end dining options. White House Subs remains a landmark for visitors and locals. Dock’s Oyster House continues to represent Atlantic City’s seafood tradition. Knife & Fork Inn stays one of the city’s strongest upscale dining names.

Weather remains important for local business. A clear or mild day can help restaurants, shops, and Boardwalk traffic, while rain, coastal wind, flooding, or rough surf can slow tourism and affect workers who depend on foot traffic.

Public safety should be covered carefully. Police statements, prosecutor releases, court filings, and official records should always be separated from rumors or scanner traffic. Viewers deserve accurate reporting, not panic.

Coming coverage: events, restaurant updates, local government decisions, public safety alerts, coastal weather, and small-business stories across Atlantic City and South Jersey.

Becoming BigRooster: The Founder Story

Founder Biography • BlackSheep Patriots News / BigRooster Media

Zachary J. Blum, known as BigRooster, built BlackSheep Patriots News from survival, loss, fatherhood, faith, mistakes, accountability, and rebuilding. The platform is not corporate-funded and it did not come from a polished boardroom. It came from real life.

The founder story matters because independent media is personal. Readers want to know who is speaking, what shaped them, and why they are willing to report hard truths. Zachary’s story includes grief, working-class survival, family loss, prison, parole, fatherhood, relocation, faith, and the choice to build something instead of quitting.

BlackSheep Patriots News is rooted in the belief that truth matters more than comfort. It is local-first, but not small-minded. It connects Atlantic City and South Jersey to national policy, weather, defense, economy, culture, faith, and accountability.

Strength Without Pretending Life Is Easy

Faith Desk • BlackSheep Patriots News

Faith does not mean life stops hurting. Faith means pain does not get the final word. A person can carry grief, regret, pressure, and uncertainty while still choosing to stand back up and keep moving with purpose.

This platform includes a faith section because news can be heavy. People need facts, but they also need strength. They need reminders that they are not powerless, not forgotten, and not finished.

Faith should not be used as a weapon. It should be a foundation: discipline, humility, gratitude, courage, service, and responsibility. A strong community needs truth, but it also needs hope.

Strait of Hormuz Watch: Oil, Shipping, Sanctions & U.S. Military Risk

Military & Defense Desk • BlackSheep Patriots News

The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world’s most important maritime chokepoints. When tension rises there, oil markets, shipping insurance, military posture, sanctions enforcement, and global supply chains can all be affected.

Public reports about Iranian tankers, shadow-fleet shipping, sanctions enforcement, and vessels being blocked or turned back should be handled carefully. A shipment being turned back is not the same as a legal seizure unless confirmed by official DOJ, Treasury, or court documents.

The Military & Defense section tracks public-source information only: CENTCOM releases, DoD statements, Navy updates, Treasury sanctions, OFAC actions, and DOJ seizure or forfeiture announcements. No classified, tactical, or real-time troop movement information belongs on the site.

Why it matters locally: oil-route disruption can affect fuel prices, shipping costs, inflation, military readiness, and household expenses.

Open Military & Defense

What the Economy Numbers Mean for Real People

Economy Desk • BlackSheep Patriots News

GDP, inflation, unemployment, jobless claims, mortgage rates, and stock indexes can sound distant, but they show up in everyday life. They affect groceries, rent, car payments, insurance, gas, hiring, layoffs, restaurant prices, and whether small businesses can survive.

A national economy can look stable on paper while families still feel pressure. That is why economic coverage should connect numbers to lived reality. Inflation is not just a percentage. It is a grocery receipt. Housing pressure is not just a mortgage chart. It is whether someone can afford to stay where they live.

For Atlantic City and South Jersey, the economy also depends on tourism, restaurants, casinos, seasonal work, construction, coastal insurance, and local transportation. A good economy section should explain both the national data and the local effect.

Open Economy Board

Food Supply Chain Watch: Prices, Recalls, Farms & Freight

Food Supply Desk • BlackSheep Patriots News

Food supply is a quality-of-life issue. Prices, recalls, trucking, fuel, ports, crop yields, livestock reports, and cold-chain movement all affect what people see at grocery stores and restaurants.

Food reporting should track both national data and local impact. USDA reports can show crop and livestock conditions. FDA and FSIS recalls show safety issues. BLS data shows price pressure. Market news and freight reports show how goods move.

In South Jersey, food supply affects restaurants, food banks, school meals, grocery access, seafood pricing, and shore-season demand. When fuel, labor, or freight costs rise, menus and household budgets feel it.

How to Read Crime News Without Getting Misled

Crime Tracker Desk • BlackSheep Patriots News

Crime coverage must be careful. An arrest is not a conviction. A charge is not proof. A scanner call is not confirmation. A viral post is not evidence. Viewers deserve clear labels and verified information.

Good crime reporting separates confirmed facts, allegations, charges, indictments, plea agreements, convictions, sentencing, and appeals. It also protects the public from rumor-driven panic.

The Crime Tracker uses official-source lanes: FBI CDE, BJS, DOJ, DEA, ATF, U.S. Marshals, local police statements, prosecutor updates, and court records. The goal is public safety and accountability, not fear.

Busboys, Comedy & Working-Class Culture

Entertainment Desk • BlackSheep Patriots News

Entertainment belongs on a news site because culture is part of public life. What people watch, laugh at, share, argue about, and quote online often reveals what audiences care about.

Busboys, comedy clips, podcasts, and viral media give the site a lighter lane next to crime, economy, defense, and government coverage. That balance matters. A site that only gives people heavy news can become exhausting. Culture keeps viewers engaged.

The entertainment section should stay rooted in the BlackSheep Patriots voice: working-class, direct, funny when appropriate, and still connected to real people.

Healthy Eating Desk GUIDE

Today's Healthy Eating Update: Push one budget meal idea today: beans or lentils, frozen vegetables, oats or brown rice, eggs/yogurt, fruit, and a small amount of olive oil. Keep medical wording general and source AHA, USDA MyPlate, Arthritis Foundation, and ALA.

Food-as-quality-of-life desk • budget-friendly whole ingredients, Mediterranean-style meals, heart-conscious choices, lung-supportive eating, arthritis-friendly anti-inflammatory patterns, and simple recipes.

Health note: This section is general education, not medical advice. Anyone with heart disease, lung disease, diabetes, kidney disease, arthritis, food allergies, pregnancy concerns, medication interactions, or a prescribed diet should check with a clinician or registered dietitian before changing their diet.

Budget baseBeansProtein, fiber, low cost
Plate model1/2 plantsVegetables + fruit focus
Heart patternMed / DASHWhole grains, fish, legumes, low sodium
InflammationOmega-3Fish, walnuts, seeds
Lung supportBalancedProtein, produce, hydration
LimitUltra-processedAdded sugar, sodium, saturated fat
🥗 Healthy Eating Desk • beans • oats • eggs • frozen vegetables • brown rice • canned tuna/salmon • olive oil • herbs • fruit • lentils • low-sodium choices • Mediterranean pattern •

Budget Whole-Ingredient Staples

Beans / Lentils

$

Use black beans, chickpeas, pinto beans, lentils, and split peas for fiber-rich protein. Rinse canned beans to reduce sodium.

Oats / Brown Rice

Base

Cheap whole-grain bases for breakfast bowls, rice bowls, soups, and leftovers.

Frozen Vegetables

Fresh-ish

Often cheaper, long-lasting, and nutritious. Use spinach, broccoli, peppers, peas, corn, or mixed vegetables.

Eggs / Yogurt

Protein

Budget protein options. Choose plain yogurt when possible and add fruit instead of extra sugar.

Canned Fish

Omega-3

Tuna, salmon, and sardines can support a Mediterranean-style pattern. Watch sodium and choose water-packed options when needed.

Olive Oil

Med

Use small amounts for cooking and dressings. A little goes a long way on a tight budget.

Fruit

Color

Bananas, apples, oranges, frozen berries, and seasonal fruit are simple snacks and dessert swaps.

Herbs / Spices

Flavor

Garlic, onion, pepper, paprika, cumin, oregano, lemon, vinegar, and herbs help reduce reliance on salt.

Simple Budget Recipes

Mediterranean Bean Bowl

Brown rice + chickpeas + cucumber/tomato or frozen veg + olive oil + lemon/vinegar + oregano + a little feta if available.

Heart-Friendly Oat Bowl

Oats + banana or frozen berries + cinnamon + spoon of peanut butter or walnuts. Skip sugary packets when possible.

Lentil Vegetable Soup

Lentils + frozen mixed vegetables + onion/garlic + low-sodium broth or water + herbs. Make a pot and eat for days.

Tuna White Bean Salad

Canned tuna + white beans + celery/onion + olive oil + lemon/vinegar + pepper. Serve on greens, toast, or rice.

Egg & Veggie Scramble

Eggs + spinach or peppers + leftover rice or potatoes. Add beans for more fiber and stretch the meal.

Sheet-Pan Chicken / Veg

Chicken thighs or beans + potatoes + carrots/onions + olive oil + herbs. Roast once, use leftovers for bowls.

Diet Pattern Options

Heart Health

Mediterranean / DASH Direction

Emphasize vegetables, fruit, whole grains, beans, fish, poultry, nuts, and unsaturated oils. Limit added sugars, excess sodium, highly processed foods, refined carbs, saturated fats, and fatty/processed meats.

Lung Issues

Balanced Fuel

For COPD, asthma, or other lung conditions, nutrition needs can vary. A balanced pattern with enough protein, fruits/vegetables, fluids as advised, and less ultra-processed food is a safer public guide than extreme diets.

Arthritis

Anti-Inflammatory Pattern

A Mediterranean-style pattern may help some people lower inflammation: fish, colorful produce, beans, nuts/seeds, olive oil, and fewer highly processed foods. Track personal triggers with a clinician.

Build-A-Plate Formula

1/2
Whole
Grain

Citizenship Data

Country / Status Board

Student Countries

Use SEVP and Open Doors to show leading sending countries, enrollment changes, school levels, OPT trends, and state/campus concentration.

J-1 Countries

Use BridgeUSA data to show countries and program categories, including summer work travel, scholars, teachers, physicians, interns, and trainees.

Visa Classes

Use State Department tables to break down F, J, H, L, B, O, P, R, E, diplomatic, crew, transit, and other nonimmigrant classes by nationality.

How Long Here

Use Census year-of-entry ranges instead of personal dates: before 2000, 2000-2009, 2010-2019, 2020 or later, depending on the table.

Dual Citizenship Reality

The U.S. generally recognizes that Americans may hold another nationality, but there is no public national registry listing every dual citizen, their other country, work, and timeline.

Public Officials Only

For elected officials, nominees, senior appointees, ambassadors, cabinet-level leaders, and public figures, this tracker may note dual-citizenship or foreign-nationality facts only when they are already reliably public, sourced, and newsworthy.

Government Workforce Data

Use OPM Federal Workforce Data for agency, location, occupation, salary band, veteran status, appointment type, and workforce trend reporting. Do not publish private employee citizenship status.

Disclosure / Ethics Watch

Use OGE public financial disclosures, Senate confirmation records, official biographies, and direct public statements for senior officials. Do not infer citizenship from name, birthplace, ethnicity, religion, spouse, family, or rumor.

Security Clearance Context

Foreign ties can matter in clearance reviews, but adjudication is individualized and not proof of wrongdoing. Report the rule framework, not accusations against private workers.

Workforce View

Use aggregate Census and labor tables to show industries and occupations for foreign-born or naturalized groups. Do not publish individual employer or job data.

Current Administration Dual-Citizenship Check

Current top officials

Verified Entries

0 listed

No current top-administration official is listed here unless a direct official biography, confirmation record, court filing, ethics disclosure, direct public statement, or credible report clearly states current dual citizenship and the other country.

Source standard

Direct Proof Required

No guesses

Birthplace, parents' country, ancestry, last name, religion, spouse, travel, language, or political position does not prove dual citizenship. The source must say citizenship or nationality directly.

Public role

Top Officials Only

Senior

This lane is limited to the President, Vice President, Cabinet, cabinet-level officials, senior White House officials, nominees, ambassadors, and elected officials where disclosure is public and newsworthy.

Public Officials Disclosure Rules

Allowed

Senior public officials, nominees, elected officeholders, and agency leaders when citizenship facts are in official records, credible interviews, court filings, confirmation material, or direct statements.

Not Allowed

Rank-and-file government workers, students, contractors, family members, neighbors, private citizens, or people identified through rumor, leaked lists, screenshots, workplace gossip, or social media claims.

Countries Listed

List another country only when the official source states the citizenship or nationality clearly. Birthplace, accent, ancestry, religion, or foreign travel does not prove citizenship.

Work Listed

Use the public office, agency role, elected position, nomination, or official biography. Avoid private employer details unless they are already part of a required public disclosure.

Publish Rules

Safe reporting line: publish counts, percentages, trends, countries, visa classes, program categories, state/county aggregates, and official source links. Do not publish private immigration status, student identity, employer identity, personal timeline, family citizenship, or individual dual-citizenship claims. Public-official citizenship notes must be limited to senior public figures where the facts are already reliably public, directly sourced, current, and newsworthy. If no direct source confirms current dual citizenship, the tracker should show zero verified entries instead of publishing a name.

Conspiracy Theory Tracker INVESTIGATING

Today's Conspiracy Tracker Watch: Promote only receipt-based items: declassified records, court filings, official hearings, agency documents, FOIA releases, and direct-source reporting. Label rumor, debate, and confirmed facts separately.

Analysis Desk • viral claims, once-dismissed topics, declassified history, official admissions, open investigations, and claims that need documents before they can be called true.

Editorial rule: This tracker does not declare a claim true because it is viral. Each item is graded by documents, hearings, court records, audits, official reports, credible expert disagreement, and what evidence would change the rating.

Conspiracy Theory Tracker • lab leak debate • Section 702 surveillance • UAP disclosure • censorship pressure claims • Epstein records • gain-of-function oversight • influence operations • MKULTRA/COINTELPRO history • FOIA watch • claims require receipts •

Viral Claims Turning Into Documented Debates

Grade A- • Documented Debate

Government Surveillance Scope

90/100

Once treated by many as fringe, broad national-security surveillance is now openly debated through FISA Section 702 reports, reauthorization fights, court oversight, and transparency releases. The live question is scope, safeguards, U.S.-person queries, and abuse prevention.

ODNI Transparency
Grade B+ • Officially Investigated

UAP / UFO Disclosure

84/100

UAP investigations, military reporting, and congressional interest are real. Unknown objects do not automatically prove non-human origin, but the existence of official UAP tracking is no longer a joke.

AARO
Grade B+ • High Public Interest

COVID Lab-Leak / Origins

82/100

The origin question moved from taboo to active government, scientific, and congressional dispute. Some official and congressional material supports a lab-incident theory; other scientists still argue for natural spillover. Track documents, not slogans.

COVID Origins
Grade B • Records Fight

Epstein Network Records

78/100

The credible issue is not internet name-dumping. It is whether sealed records, court files, flight logs, financial records, plea-deal history, and agency decisions reveal protected networks or institutional failures.

DOJ
Grade B • Platform Pressure

Government / Platform Censorship

76/100

Public debate now centers on whether officials pressured platforms, flagged lawful speech, or crossed constitutional lines. Separate direct coercion from ordinary government communication and platform policy choices.

SCOTUS Case
Grade B • Proven Category

Foreign Influence Operations

86/100

State-backed influence campaigns, bot networks, hacking-and-leak operations, and propaganda lanes are documented. Each viral example still needs attribution evidence before blaming a country, party, or agency.

Foreign Interference
Grade B- • Oversight Needed

Gain-of-Function Funding

74/100

The real investigation lane is grant oversight, risk review, biosafety rules, subcontracting, and what U.S. agencies knew. Avoid claiming intent without documents; follow funding records and hearing exhibits.

EcoHealth Report
Grade A • Declassified History

MKULTRA / Human Experiments

95/100

This is the cautionary history file: government-linked experimentation and covert programs are not imaginary in the historical record. Use it as proof that oversight matters, not proof that every new claim is true.

CIA Reading Room
Grade A • Declassified History

COINTELPRO / Domestic Disruption

94/100

Historic domestic surveillance and disruption programs were documented and investigated. This belongs in the tracker because yesterday's records explain why today's accountability questions matter.

FBI Vault

Proof Test Before Publishing

1. What Is Claimed?

Write the exact claim in one sentence. Do not upgrade a possibility into a fact.

2. What Is Confirmed?

List records, filings, official statements, data, named sources, and what is still missing.

3. Who Benefits?

Ask who gains money, power, cover, attention, or legal protection if the claim spreads.

4. What Would Disprove It?

A strong investigation names the evidence that would lower confidence, not only raise it.
